At a glance

Lower Burrell had 11,758 residents in the 2020 census, and its median household income, $84,602, is the highest of the three cities. It was split off from Burrell Township in 1879 and became a city in 1959. The map data holds 5,857 buildings, 5,527 address points and 419 listed places in the city.

Sources: Data USA, Pittsburgh Post-Gazette

Safety

Lower Burrell police reported 10 violent crimes to the FBI in 2024, or 0.9 per 1,000 residents and about 0.8 a month, down from 17 in the 11 months of 2023 it reported (about 1.5 a month). That is the lowest rate since 2018 (0.8). Property crime fell to 2.3 per 1,000, the lowest in the department's FBI record, which goes back to 2000. Police cleared all 10 violent crimes.

8 news-reported incidents in Lower Burrell are on the police blotter, the earliest from 2018.

Serious crashes

PennDOT recorded 73 crashes in Lower Burrell from 2005 through 2024 that killed or seriously injured someone. They killed 22 people and seriously injured 69.

Neighborhoods and landmarks

A third-class city since Jan. 12, 1959, split from Burrell Township in 1879. It covers 11.52 square miles and had 11,758 residents in 2020. Informal neighborhoods: Bon Air, Braeburn, Braeburn Heights, Central City, Edgecliff, Gladeview, Indian Fields I & II and Kinloch. Its business district overlaps Bon Air, Central City and Gladeview.

Source: Wikipedia

History

1852

Burrell Township formed.

Burrell Township was carved out of Allegheny Township by court order and named for Judge Jeremiah Murry Burrell of the Westmoreland County Court.

Source: City of Lower Burrell

1879

Lower and Upper Burrell split.

Burrell Township was divided into two townships, Lower Burrell and Upper Burrell.

Source: Pittsburgh Post-Gazette

1890

'Kensington' planned.

The Burrell Improvement Company picked the level riverfront land south of Lower Burrell for a new city and named it 'Kensington'. The name was later changed to 'New Kensington' to avoid postal confusion with the Philadelphia neighborhood.

Source: Wikipedia

1959

Lower Burrell becomes a city.

Lower Burrell was incorporated as a third-class city on Jan. 12, 1959.

Source: Pittsburgh Post-Gazette

2020

Population 12,170.

The 2020 census counted 12,170 New Kensington residents, 4,772 in Arnold and 11,758 in Lower Burrell.

Source: Wikipedia

2021

Fridays on Fifth and St. Patrick's parade begin.

The monthly Fridays on Fifth food-truck night started downtown in 2021. Lower Burrell's St. Patrick's Day parade was started during the COVID-19 lockdown.

Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)
